uncited: It solves the problem of converting continuous or sparse input data into a structured grid where each voxel stores specific attributes (density, velocity, size, or directional normals) required for Direct Volume Rendering (DVR) or simulation.

It differs from its siblings by encompassing both the geometric occupancy determination (e.g., [Interior Voxelize](995-interior-voxelize.md)) and the assignment of physical or visual attributes (e.g., [Velocity Voxelization](3082-velocity-voxelization.md), [Anisotropic Voxelization](4331-anisotropic-voxelization.md)) to those voxels, rather than just binary occupancy.
- **Definition**: A volumetric attribute not directly derived from intensity, but calculated on pre-segmented parts of a volume.
